diagram_candidates.claim: The vertices are right cosets Hg, the base vertex is H, and each generator x gives a directed edge Hg → Hgx; traversing backward reads x⁻¹.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: This definition names the graph's vertex, basepoint, oriented generator edges and inverse traversal rule. A small correctly labeled example can make the right-coset convention and path endpoint formula concrete.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: For the rank-one free group F(a) and subgroup H=<a²>, draw the two right cosets H and Ha, with basepoint H and directed a-labeled edges H→Ha and Ha→H. Mark backward traversal as a^{-1} and verify the path endpoint rule against right multiplication. The subgroup has index two, so these are exactly the two vertices.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The abstract edge rule and endpoint formula are explicit in the source. This concrete index-two example is consistent with F(a)≅Z and H=2Z; no defect in the current definition was found.

diagram_candidates.claim: For an oriented quotient edge from v to w, its stabilizer G_e embeds into both endpoint stabilizers G_v and G_w, and changing representatives conjugates all three by the same group element.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The result is precisely two inclusions attached to the two ends of an oriented edge, together with simultaneous conjugacy under representative change. A diagram can display the orientation and the two maps at once.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw one oriented edge e:v→w; place G_e below the edge and arrows G_e↪G_v and G_e↪G_w to the origin and terminus stabilizers. Add a second representative e'=h·e with v'=h·v,w'=h·w and conjugation labels h(−)h⁻¹ on each stabilizer, preserving the same inclusion directions.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: Source lines 32–40 give the inclusions and lines 54–56 prove representative change conjugates each subgroup by h. The proposed orientation and maps follow those explicit claims; no existing diagram or mathematical defect was found.

diagram_candidates.claim: Relative to a maximal subtree T, reduced closed graph-of-groups words represent elements; positive edge length is nonidentity, while an edge-length-zero word is identity exactly when its vertex-group coefficient is identity.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The proof distinguishes tree edges, which are killed in the relative fundamental group, from non-tree edges, which become HNN stable letters, and uses edge-group embeddings at incident vertices. A diagram can connect the graph-of-groups data to the amalgam/HNN alternatives driving the induction.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw a minimal graph with two vertex groups joined by a maximal-tree edge and one additional loop edge; mark T, label the tree edge as amalgamating the incident edge-group images, and label the non-tree loop's stable letter plus its two associated edge-group embeddings. Show reduced edge paths and indicate that an immediate reversal is allowed only when the intervening coefficient lies in the relevant edge-group image. Keep orientations consistent with the source's edge reversal and HNN conventions.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The tree-edge/amalgam and non-tree-edge/HNN branches are explicit in lines 54–60. A diagram would summarize those cases; no issue with the written maps or orientations was established.
